Motivation
Named groups are how the JVM describes TLS key exchange schemes. APIs to use named groups have been added in Java 20.
ViaJEP 527: Post-Quantum Hybrid Key Exchange for TLS 1.3, new key exchange schemes resistant to quantum attacks, usually referred to as Post Quantum Cryptography (PQC), are being introduced. This JEP was initially delivered in Java 27. It's being backported by several implementations to earlier Java versions. Note that theSSLParameters.setNamedGroups()API is available from Java 20, but the PQC named groups themselves (e.g.x25519_mlkem768) require Java 27 or a vendor backport that includes JEP 527.
Due to threats like "harvest now, decrypt later", many organizations are now actively considering PQC TLS. It is also mandated by several governments and industries such as finance, healthcare and defense.
Public Interfaces
All communication channels that are encrypted via TLS need to support PQC. This includes:
Client to broker/controller
Broker/controller to client
Broker/controller to broker/controller
Connect workers accepting REST traffic
Connect worker to Connect worker
OAuth token retrieval (client)
OAuth JWKS retrieval (server)
To cover all these scenarios, a single configuration can be used:
Name: ssl.named.groups
Type: List
Default: Empty, the default JVM named groups are used
Description: An ordered list of key exchange named groups to use for SSL connections, with the most preferred group first. The supported values depend on the SSL provider and Java runtime.
It can be set in clients, servers, Streams instances and Connect worker configurations. For example:
On servers, it can also be set per listener, for example:
For OAuth it must be set viasasl.jaas.configor a JAAS file, for example:
If the configuration is set and the JVM does not support the named groups APIs, aConfigExceptionwill be thrown at startup.
If the configuration is set to unknown named groups, the failure happens when the TLS connection is established. This is the same behavior as withssl.cipher.suites.
If the configuration is set, like withssl.cipher.suites, a TLS connection can only be established when the client and server share at least one named group.
The TLS version (set via ssl.protocol) gates what named groups are valid and automatically drops entries not compatible (like for ciphers).
Proposed Changes
The named groups APIs are only available in Java 20+. Because the Kafka modules still support Java 11 (clients) and Java 17 (servers), logic trying to set named groups will use reflection so it compiles with the currently supported Java versions.
Clients/Servers
TheDefaultSslEngineFactoryclass handles the TLS logic for clients and brokers. Ifssl.named.groupsis set, theSSLParameters.setNamedGroups()method will be called via reflection.
OAuth
The OAuth/OIDC implementation makes two types of outbound HTTPS connections to the identity provider:
Token retrieval (client-side):OAuthBearerLoginCallbackHandlerusesHttpJwtRetrieverto fetch JWT access tokens from the token endpoint. Every Kafka client (producer, consumer, admin) and broker (for inter-broker OAuth) makes this call on each token refresh.
JWKS key retrieval (broker-side):OAuthBearerValidatorCallbackHandlerusesVerificationKeyResolverFactoryto periodically fetch the identity provider's public keys from the JWKS endpoint, which are used to verify JWT signatures.
TheJaasOptionsUtils.createSSLSocketFactory()method will be updated to wrap the returnedSSLSocketFactoryso thatSSLParameters(including named groups, cipher suites, and enabled protocols) are applied to each socket after creation, mirroring whatDefaultSslEngineFactorydoes for clients and servers.
Connect REST API
Connect uses Jetty to expose its REST API for users and for worker-to-worker communications.
